routes.label: Pick the shelf lock
Talk Rook out of his spares
Notice his pocket, then talk

get.journal: Rook, who keeps the test yard, wants his lockpicks from a jammed shelf.

routes.label: Take Elder Halloran's order to Bram
Talk Bram through a manual cycle
Pay Bram in circuit boards
Shame Bram into it
Crawl the maintenance shaft

wake.journal: A stranger hammered on the great door before dawn — the first outsider in living memory — and died before he could speak. Doc Pell has the body. Elder Halloran is waiting for me.

objectives.text: See the body in the clinic

door.journal: Halloran wants me to go outside and find out who he was, and why he carried my face. Bram Coyle keeps the great door, and he does not want to open it.

objectives.text: Get the great door open — or find another way out
Get something better than a shiv

leave.journal: The way out is open. Whatever is out there, it has been waiting ninety years.

done.journal: I left Cistern 9. The track north leads to Shale, the nearest town, if the old maps are right — and the stranger came from somewhere.

news.text: someone walked out of the old shelter at the salt cut

routes.label: Ask Sheriff Vey; she saw him
Buy the rumour from Mags or Pike
Read his tracks on the west road
Read the notebook line (Archive Clerk)
Earn Hollis Crane's goodwill and ask him

road.journal: He walked west for weeks on a wound that should have killed him, and he came to our door on purpose. Shale is the only town for a day in any direction. Someone there will have seen an old man with a bad hip.

objectives.text: Learn where he went from here

overpass.journal: He went to the Rust Dogs under the overpass, and he went knowing what they were. Whatever he carried, he meant to trade it there — and he reached us with only the photograph.

done.journal: I found the Rust Dogs' camp under the dead highway. If he traded here, Kessler has what he traded.

routes.label: Buy it from Kessler (80 Tolls or the bolt rifle)
Win it at Dust
Convince Kessler the paper is a danger (Pike reported him)
Carry his tribute terms to Shale
Wren steals it for a place at your side
Lift it from under his lamp at night
Vasha's coup: kill Kessler in his hall
Wren's exodus, with the sheriff's word

camp.journal: He traded the paper to Kessler for water. Kessler can't read it, won't sell it to the Tollmen, and keeps it under his lamp. There are more ways into a thing like that than through the front of it.

objectives.text: Talk to the scout who found him

done.journal: The map is mine: twelve places pricked on a road, and beside each a block of marks I can't read. Yet.

routes.label: Pay the debt (Kessler 60, or Perpetua 40)
Trade Kessler the tribute errand for him
Pick the cage at night
Take him out by force

held.journal: Mags's partner Teo Marsh is in the Rust Dogs' cage over a debt he says isn't his. The Dogs want sixty Tolls or something better.

home.journal: Teo is out. He is walking home to Shale on legs he doesn't trust.

done.journal: Teo is back behind the bar, counting. Mags has not stopped shouting at him, which is how she says thank you.

routes.label: Pay the tithe (or let Shale pay it)
Carry Kessler's terms and have the sheriff accept them
Talk Vasha down to nothing
Cut the Dogs' truck at the overpass beforehand
Fight beside the militia

due.journal: Twice a year the Rust Dogs come into Shale for a tithe of water and drink, and twice a year Shale pays it and hates itself. The next one is days away. Everyone knows the day; nobody says it.

objectives.text: Hear what the sheriff means to do
Put Kessler's terms to the sheriff
Do something about the Dogs' truck

day.journal: They are here. Vasha Kade and four Dogs at the wells, and the whole town leaning toward them the way it leans toward the pumps.

objectives.text: Face the Dogs at the wells

paid.journal: Shale paid. The water went up the west road on the Dogs' cart, and nobody died, and the sheriff has not looked at anyone since.

negotiated.journal: Half of what they took last time, in water, and Vasha Kade walked out of Shale with less than she came for. She will remember whose doing that was.

sabotaged.journal: They walked in and they walked out, carrying what they could carry, which was not much. Vasha knows somebody cut the truck. She does not know who. Yet.

fought.journal: Shale fought. The street is quiet and the wells are Shale's, and the price of that is going to arrive from the overpass one night soon.

news.text: Shale fought the Rust Dogs at the wells on Tribute Day and held them off

settled.journal: Tribute Day came and went without me. Shale paid, and Deputy Reese took a beating for arguing the count. People have noticed who was not there.

routes.label: Work the cipher yourself
Read it as record shorthand (Archive Clerk)
Buy the Tollmen's cipher wheel from Pike
Hollis Crane knows the hand

cipher.journal: Twelve places on a road, a block of marks beside each, and the nearest pin is Shale. Somebody can read this: a clerk, a drifter who has seen the hand, the Tollmen who sell keys to everything — or me, with time and a crib.

objectives.text: Read the first name on the map
Get a key to the cipher

read.journal: Jonah Reese. Shale. Within the month, the list says, and does not say how. A man walked across the waste to bring me a list with the deputy's name on it, and mine was never on it at all — or it is, further east, where the road goes.

decision.text: Chapter One ended with the first name read: Jonah Reese, within the month.

news.text: the salt-cut stranger has been asking what the deputy's name is worth

routes.label: Pay the toll (20 Tolls)
Carry a sealed guild packet east (free passage, and a catch)
Show a forged pass (Teo or Perpetua can make one)
Climb the chain-link at the wall's north end, at night
Stamp yourself through on the gate terminal
Hit the Tollhouse with Vasha's Dogs

road.journal: The stranger's road runs east, and east of Shale the only road is the old highway, and the highway belongs to the Tollmen. Tollhouse 9 sits across it like a hand held up. Two days' walk.

objectives.text: The guild's outriders ride this road. Find out who shot him

through.journal: Through the wall, one way or another. The guild thanks you for your custom, or will send someone to count what you cost it. The highway runs east toward a hill with a mast on it — the next pin on the map.

news.text: someone from the salt cut went east through Tollhouse 9

routes.label: Read the ledger when the booth is empty (after nine at night)
Read it under the clerk's nose
Get the outriders to say it themselves

rumour.journal: Pike "reported" the stranger to the guild, as per. The guild keeps books. If the outriders who shot him were paid, Tollhouse 9 wrote it down.

objectives.text: Find the entry in the Tollhouse 9 ledger

known.journal: The guild paid two outriders to put the stranger down on the highway, on a Factor's word from Shale. You know it; you cannot yet prove it to anyone who matters.

objectives.text: Take the ledger page as proof

evidence.journal: A page in your pack says Factor Pike paid for a killing. Shale's sheriff would want it. Pike would pay to have it back. Either way, it is worth more than paper.

objectives.text: Show the page to Sheriff Vey

shown.journal: Ada Vey read the page twice and folded it into her shirt. Pike is still at his post. Shale is a small town and the guild is not; but the sheriff knows now what the guild is for.

sold.journal: Pike bought his own page back, courteously, at the posted rate, and burned it in front of you. He will remember the courtesy. So will the guild.

routes.label: Pay the Hollow their track toll (or a circuit board)
Tell the Hollow the voice is your problem
Climb the gully past the camp
Clear the track
Read the relay's traffic log
Listen through a grid link

track.journal: The next pin on the map is a hill with a mast, a day east of Tollhouse 9 and north of the highway. The guild does not go up there. Something up there still answers the city.

objectives.text: Find the track to Signal Hill
Get past the camp on the track

station.journal: A dead station with a live relay and a voice that reads the same list every night. Whatever the stranger's map is, this is where it is read from.

objectives.text: Find out what the relay still answers
Listen to the voice in the station

done.journal: The relay at Signal Hill talks to something east and relays a nightly list west — to a pump station in the Sallow marked DW-4. Dry Wells. The map's road runs back toward home before it runs on.

routes.label: Cut the speaker
Put it on the mast for the whole Sallow
Leave it reading

voice.journal: The voice in the station is reading the stranger's list aloud: the overpass, Kessler, day forty-five, killed by Vasha's hand. It will read it every night to nobody — unless it reads it to everybody.

silenced.journal: The speaker is cut. The list is still being sent; nobody on this hill will hear it read again.

amplified.journal: Every dead radio in the Sallow says the same five words at night now. The overpass will have heard it by morning. Kessler will have heard it. So will Vasha.

routes.label: Change the conditions of the fall (the windpump tower)
Change the conditions of the fight (drill the militia)
Change the conditions of the fever (the east cistern)
Do nothing, and see what the list does

month.journal: Jonah Reese, Shale, within the month. The list did not say how. Shale is full of ways for an earnest young man to die — a fall, a fight, a fever — and if one road is blocked, whatever wrote his name will look for another. Prevention means changing the conditions. There is no clock to race: the month, whatever the list means by it, will not be over before the business east of here is settled.

objectives.text: Find out how a deputy spends his days and nights
Change the conditions of the fall
Change the conditions of the fight
Change the conditions of the fever

fell.journal: The month was out before you were back. Jonah Reese went up the windpump tower for the vane, the way he did every week, and a rung let go. Shale buried him behind the sheriff's office. The militia is four rifles again. The list was right.

decision.text: Jonah Reese died before the month was out, as the list said: a fall from the windpump tower.

news.text: Deputy Reese fell from the windpump tower

data.text:
THE MONTH
THE LIST WAS RIGHT

fought.journal: The month was out before you were back. Jonah Reese walked the east street alone at midnight, the way he did, and four Dogs came in off the salt for nothing in particular. Shale buried him behind the sheriff's office. The militia is four rifles again. The list was right.

decision.text: Jonah Reese died before the month was out, as the list said: alone on the east street, against the Dogs.

news.text: Deputy Reese was killed on the east street by Rust Dogs in the night

data.text:
THE MONTH
THE LIST WAS RIGHT

fevered.journal: The month was out before you were back. Jonah Reese drank last from the east cistern, the way the ration said, and the fever took four days to do what the tower and the Dogs had not. Shale buried him behind the sheriff's office. The militia is four rifles again. The list was right.

decision.text: Jonah Reese died before the month was out, as the list said: a fever from the east cistern.

news.text: Deputy Reese died of a fever from the east cistern

data.text:
THE MONTH
THE LIST WAS RIGHT

lived.journal: The month is out, and Jonah Reese is alive. The tower, the street and the cistern each had their conditions changed, and the list — for the first time anyone knows of — was wrong. Whatever wrote it will have noticed.

decision.text: Jonah Reese lived out the month. The first forecast anyone knows of was broken.

news.text: the deputy is alive past the month, and people are counting

data.text:
THE MONTH
THE LIST WAS WRONG

routes.label: Dawn and dusk in the yard until nine rifles shoot
The drunk behind the yard: shame him sober, or take him east

drill.journal: Nine rifles, four that shoot. Drills at dawn and dusk with rounds Shale cannot spare, and from the first night nobody walks the street alone. Corporal Lind says a man who used to be the best shot in the Sallow drinks behind the yard.

objectives.text: Drill them until nine rifles shoot

done.journal: Nine rifles that shoot, pairs on the street at night, and Ada's signature on it. Shale is not safer; it is less alone.

routes.label: Override the schedule at the console
The pump man's credential: Oriel Marr's key and her father's word
Break the governor under the gauges
Sell the console to Factor Pike
The pump man's diary has the word on its first page
Leave the schedule as it is

track.journal: The line from Signal Hill runs west to a pump station marked DW-4: Dry Wells, a day east of Shale on a track nobody uses. Whatever sets Shale's water sits there. Somebody is living there too; the Tollmen call them ghosts.

objectives.text: Get past the rifle on the approach

station.journal: The shacks are the family's; the station is Oriel Marr's; the room at the east end of the pump hall is locked and hums, and her father's key is on a cord round her neck. A lock can be picked and a door can be forced, and the family will remember which.

objectives.text: Open the room at the end of the station

console.journal: DW-4 holds Shale at 0.62 of something, on a schedule changed from upstream. The console will take a new number from someone who can make it listen, or from the pump man's word; the governor under the gauges can be broken; Factor Pike would pay to hold what the console holds; or the schedule can be left as it is, which is also a choice. Whatever is decided here, the Sallow's business is done with and the road runs east.

objectives.text: Find the line that is held constant

restored.journal: SHALE — 1.00. The pumps run outside the clock now, and the last line in the station's log is yours. Shale will drink; something upstream will read the line. The road runs east.

decision.text: You set Shale's allocation at Dry Wells to the full measure.

data.text:
ACT ONE ENDS
THE WATER CLOCK

news.text: the pumps in the yard run twice as long as they did, and nobody changed anything in Shale

freed.journal: The governor is in pieces and the pumps run flat out, for Shale, until the aquifer or the bearings give up. The console has stopped pretending to know. The road runs east.

decision.text: You broke the governor at Dry Wells: Shale has all the water, for as long as it lasts.

data.text:
ACT ONE ENDS
THE WATER CLOCK

news.text: the pumps have not stopped since the night the salt-cut stranger came back from the east, and the north tank is overflowing into the street

sold.journal: Factor Pike has the console, a guild engineer has the chair, and Shale's water is sold by the measure, reliably. You have a hundred and fifty Tolls and a seat on a guild caravan east.

decision.text: You sold the Dry Wells console to the Tollmen for a hundred and fifty Tolls.

data.text:
ACT ONE ENDS
THE WATER CLOCK

news.text: the Tollmen have put an engineer on the Dry Wells station and water in the yard is sold by the measure

kept.journal: SHALE — 0.62. You stood in front of the thing that sets Shale's water and left it as it was. Shale thins on schedule, and whatever changed the number can change it back, and nothing upstream has noticed you. The road runs east.

decision.text: You left the Dry Wells schedule as you found it.

data.text:
ACT ONE ENDS
THE WATER CLOCK

routes.label: Talk Sheriff Vey into taking them under her law
Pay their way east
Leave them on their trickle and say nothing

squat.journal: Five people live in the scrap shacks at Dry Wells on a trickle tapped off Shale's line: three generations out of a cistern that failed. Shale does not know they exist; the Tollmen call them ghosts. Oriel Marr will go to Shale if the sheriff says yes and means it; she will take forty Tolls for the road; or she will stay, if nobody tells Shale about the valve.

objectives.text: Ask Sheriff Vey whether Shale would have them
Settle what becomes of the family

shale.journal: The Marrs walked to Shale under Sheriff Vey's law and got the old tannery. Juno has a second street; Cato has no valve; Oriel has a chair that was built for sitting. Shale is five people bigger and does not know yet what that costs.

moved.journal: The Marrs took forty Tolls and the road east: the windpump graveyard, then the glass. Oriel's father walked it the other way. The shacks at Dry Wells are empty, and the valve is shut.

left.journal: The Marrs stay at Dry Wells on their trickle, and Shale was told nothing. When Shale comes, it comes; it was always going to.

shot.journal: You drew on the family at Dry Wells. What is left of them stays, because there is nowhere else, and Oriel Marr gave you the key with nothing in her voice at all.

routes.label: Open the cab
Wake the machine for Shale
Sell the controller to Factor Pike
Leave it sleeping and keep the controller

found.journal: A guild convoy truck on its side on the white pan, its skid half a mile long, its cab locked, and in a ring pressed into the crust beside it a machine the size of a dog that has not moved since it sat down. Something came down here, took the crew, and left that.

objectives.text: Find out what the convoy was carrying
Decide what the machine is for

shale.journal: The machine stood up for you and walked to Shale at your heel, and sits in the sheriff's yard now, and nothing comes into the town at night that it does not look at first. Somewhere east, whoever made it will want to know where it went.

sold.journal: Factor Pike has the controller and the guild will have the machine. A hundred and fifty Tolls, and the knowledge that the Tollmen now own something that can stand up.

kept.journal: The machine sleeps in its ring on the pan, and the slab that wakes it is in your pack, warm. Nobody east knows that yet.

routes.label: Read the wall
Talk them into sitting down
Wren knows their names

thefts.journal: Twice a week something comes over the north wall of the Choir's orchard and takes the green fruit, which nobody takes. Brother Anselm wants it to stop and does not want anyone hurt, and knows those are two different things.

objectives.text: Find out who comes over it
Wait for them by the beds after the lamps are out

choir.journal: Kip and Mote sleep in the Choir's tents now and eat first. The overpass has two fewer mouths and will decide later whether that was a theft.

returned.journal: You walked the two of them back to the overpass in the dark. Whoever is short there is shorter; the Dogs remember who brought their children home; the wall will be robbed again when they are hungry.

cell.journal: Two children in Sheriff Vey's cell, with blankets, while she sends to the overpass and the overpass decides whether they are its. Anselm asked you not to hurt them, and meant something larger.

let_go.journal: They went over the wall with the sack. Anselm leaves the green ones on the wall now and calls it a tithe. The sky is open; so is the wall.

routes.label: Keep the wagon in your eye to Tollhouse 9

ride.journal: The Wheel's salt wagon goes to Tollhouse 9 with the Tollmen's caravan, and the guild's guards guard the guild's wagons. Walk the Tollhouse road from Shale beside it; whatever the road asks for, it is asking the Wheel. Sixty Tolls at the gate.

paid.journal: The salt is weighed at the gate and the Wheel's wagon goes in on the guild's count. Sixty Tolls, and the Wheel remembers who rode.

news.text: The Wheel's salt got to the Tollhouse with a stranger walking beside it.

routes.label: Sell the Cistern's seed to the guild
Put it under the open sky with the Choir

fetch.journal: Factor Pike buys viable seed at absurd prices, in advance, for a client east of the Teeth he will not name. Cistern 9 kept a seed bank for ninety years; the Elder keeps its key. The guild would pay a great deal. The Choir would plant it.

objectives.text: Get a case of viable seed from the Cistern

deliver.journal: The case is cold in your pack. Pike at the Tollmen post pays in Tolls and standing; Sister Calla or Brother Anselm would put it in the ground.

sold.journal: The guild has the Cistern's seed, and a client east of the Teeth will have it after them. The Tolls were real. So was the look on Calla's face when she heard.

given.journal: The Cistern's seed is in the Choir's beds under the open sky. Pike heard, and wrote something in a ledger. Anselm says the first beans in a fortnight.

routes.label: See to the sick in the mission tent

tend.journal: Sister Calla has three on cots and one of her: a dust-lung, a broken arm, a fever. She will take any pair of hands that can hold a cup steady.

objectives.text: See to the old man with the dust-lung
See to the girl with the broken arm
See to the man with the fever

tended.journal: Three seen to. Calla will want to say something about it; she usually does.

done_stage.journal: The Choir calls you a lay healer now, which Calla says is a way of saying they trust your hands. What you did about the girl is between you and the sky.

routes.label: Tell the sheriff who owns the saloon
Make silence worth something
Make the books balance for her

audit.journal: Mags has handed you two ledgers and a night's room for reading them. She says it is to catch a thieving barman. Read them.

decide.journal: The second ledger's margins are in a guild hand. The Dry Well is held against a Tollmen loan Mags cannot pay, and the buyout is signed: on paper the saloon is Pike's, and the town does not know. She wants it to stay that way.

clean.journal: Two ledgers, water in and water out. If there is a thief, it is not in the numbers. Mags paid you twenty and looked relieved about the wrong thing.

exposed.journal: Shale knows the Dry Well is guild property. Mags will not pour for you again. Ada says the town needed to know and does not look as if she enjoyed it.

squeezed.journal: A hundred and fifty Tolls, and Mags's silence bought with hers. She remembers it every time she sees you.

helped.journal: The books balance now, in a way that will survive a guild clerk's lamp. The room upstairs is yours for nothing, for as long as there is a Dry Well.

routes.label: Carry back the truth
Carry back a kindness

carry.journal: Bram gave you a letter sealed with machine grease, for a woman called Edda Vale in Shale. He asked you not to read it. He did not say how he knows her.

answer.journal: Edda Vale has been under the salt six years. Her daughter Hesper read the letter and went quiet for a long time. Something has to go back to the Cistern.

objectives.text: Take an answer back to Bram

truth.journal: Bram knows. He thanked you, which was worse than if he had not.

kind.journal: Bram has a letter from Edda Vale that Edda Vale did not write. He reads it at the machine when he thinks nobody is looking. He is happier than he was. You will have to live with the rest.

routes.label: Buy the line from the Grand Factor (she sells everything, not at that price)
Talk your way to the Grand Factor's desk and make her say it
Read the Exchange ledgers after the floor closes, or under the clerk's nose
Pull the protection account off the board
An old trader at the Span knows what the paper means, and what the packet was

road.journal: The stranger's road runs east off the map's edge, past the Tollhouse, over the glass, to a bridge with a town on it — Ninebridge, where the guild keeps its Exchange and, the caravan woman said, sells things that have not happened yet. If the outriders who shot him were paid, they were paid from there.

objectives.text: Find who paid for the outriders
Deliver the sealed packet to the Exchange

paid.journal: Paid from the floor. The Exchange at Ninebridge bought the stranger's death the way it buys everything: two riders, four days, a line in a ledger, by order of the floor. The guild sells paper that says what will happen, and someone was selling them the paper. The road runs on east, to the farms and the city, and the map's next pins.

decision.text: You learned at Ninebridge that the Exchange paid the outriders who shot the stranger.

news.text: someone from the salt cut was asking after the protection account on the Exchange floor

routes.label: Buy her contract at the block (the price rises with the crowd)
Take the contract from the auctioneer's box, or cut the cage at night
The auctioneer hates his work. Give him a reason to lose a lot
Wren knows her

block.journal: The auction block on Ninebridge's east bank sells debt: whoever holds a contract holds the debtor until it clears. Today's lot four is a young woman called Sable, nineteen, fifty-eight Tolls and interest. Fen will open at sixty.

objectives.text: Settle lot four, one way or another

freed.journal: Sable Calloway walked off the block with her paper in her own hand, which is the only place a debt contract is worth nothing. She said she would go west, to Shale, where a sister might be, and that she would not thank you, and then did.

news.text: a debtor walked off the Ninebridge block free, and the auctioneer called it a sale

kept.journal: You hold Sable Calloway's contract. Fifty-eight Tolls and interest, service until cleared. She keeps the berth at the Span swept and does not look at you, and the paper is in your pack, and you could tear it up any morning.

decision.text: You bought Sable Calloway's debt at Ninebridge and kept it.

resold.journal: You bought Sable Calloway's contract at sixty and sold it to the floor at ninety. The clerk did not ask where she was going. Thirty Tolls, and a sister somewhere who will hear.

decision.text: You bought and resold a debtor's contract at Ninebridge for the margin.

news.text: someone bought lot four at the Ninebridge block and sold her on the same day

sold_on.journal: Lot four went to a guild buyer at ninety, the way lots do. You watched. The crowd moved to lot five.

decision.text: You watched Sable Calloway sold at the Ninebridge block and did nothing.

routes.label: Break the stoppage for the guild (they pay eighty)
Pick up a strap and carry with them until the guild comes to the table
The guild holds a forecast that says the porters lose. Put it in their hands
Pay the difference yourself and shame the guild into matching it

camp.journal: The porters who carry Ninebridge's goods up the ramps have sat down with their straps off: a share of the bridge toll, or nothing moves. The toll-warden says they will be back on the third day. He says it like a man reading.

objectives.text: End the stoppage, one way or another

broken.journal: The porters put their straps back on for the guild's terms, on the day the paper said. Eighty Tolls, the warden's nod, and forty people who know your face.

news.text: the Ninebridge porters went back under the guild's terms; a stranger talked them down

won.journal: The guild came to the table. A tenth of the crossing goes to the porters now — the first time, Voss says, that the bridge has paid the backs that carry it. The warden has a new rate painted, and a new face when he sees you.

news.text: the Ninebridge porters won a share of the bridge toll

routes.label: The sick in the long hall: fever, or something they drank
Test the two troughs at the well
Follow the night tracks from the well
Old Benedek saw a light at the well. Get him to say whose
Wait by the well after midnight

rows.journal: Openfield: the Choir's farms in the glass, and every third row dying. The Elder calls it blight and does not believe himself. The road east runs through here, and so does the map's; and a man at Openfield, Calla said, knows more about the word the stranger died saying.

objectives.text: Find what is killing the rows

found.journal: Not blight. The north trough is dosed every night by the Elder's own son, who has read a guild forecast until it fell apart: Openfield burns if its harvest rises above plan, so he keeps it below. What you do with that is the whole of Openfield.

exposed.journal: You told the Elder. He heard it the way a man hears his own name read from a list, and then he walked his son to the track and did not come back for an hour. The well is clean. The rows will come back. Mason will not. The road runs on east, to a dead shelter and the city.

decision.text: You told Elder Mason that his son was poisoning Openfield's well.

news.text: the Elder of Openfield cast out his own son over the well

mercy.journal: Tobias stopped. You hold his secret and his sheet, and the Elder holds a theory about blight that he can go on not believing. The well is clean by the week's end. The rows will come back. The road runs on east, to a dead shelter and the city.

decision.text: You let Tobias Mason stop poisoning the well without telling his father.

unwritten.journal: You gave Tobias to Petra, and the Unwritten took him down the hatch to argue about whether a man who breaks a forecast by starving his own people is one of them or the opposite. The Elder thinks his son went east. The well is clean. The road runs on east, to a dead shelter and the city.

decision.text: You handed Tobias Mason to the Unwritten.

dead.journal: Tobias Mason died at his own well with a knife in his hand. The Choir buried him under the open sky and did not sing. The well is clean. Nothing else here is. The road runs on east.

decision.text: Tobias Mason died at Openfield's well.

news.text: the Elder's son died at the well in Openfield; a stranger's hand was in it

routes.label: Wait in the seed store after dark
The tally: counted, not grabbed. Someone with a key
The guild's hand on the lane buys what the Choir won't sell
Let the thief keep stealing — dead seed

count.journal: A crate of viable seed walks out of Openfield's store every night: counted at dusk, short at dawn, no broken lock. Keeper Doria has stopped sleeping.

exposed.journal: Hollin Brannock, who came from the Sump with nothing and was given the yard, carried a crate a night to the guild's hand for twelve Tolls each. Doria wanted him gone. The Elder gave him the yard back and the night watch, which is a Choir punishment and worse than the track.

chaff.journal: The guild's hand left Openfield with six crates of seed that will grow nothing anywhere, bought at a future's price, and a receipt. Doria laughed for the first time in a month. Somewhere east of the Teeth a client will plant it and wait.

decision.text: You let the Tollmen buy dead seed from Openfield at a living price.

news.text: the guild bought Choir seed by night at Openfield and got chaff with manners

cut.journal: A crate a night still walks, and a tenth of each walks to you. Doria counts, and the Elder calls it blight of a different kind, and nobody says your name.

decision.text: You took a cut of the seed stolen from Openfield for the guild.

gone.journal: Corso Vail took his coin and his future-paper back down the track to Ninebridge. The store is whole at dawn. Hollin keeps the yard and his tent and the look of a man who has been let off once.

routes.label: Raise a cairn for someone you lost, under the open sky

asked.journal: The Choir's door is a burial: raise a cairn in the ground under the windpump for someone you have lost, with Petra Mason saying the words, and you are a sister or brother of the Open Sky — which opens the long halls, and other doors.

objectives.text: Raise a cairn at the burial ground

done.journal: A cairn under the windpump with no name on it, and a stone from it in your pack. Sister, or brother, of the Open Sky. The Choir's halls are open to you from Shale to the city.

decision.text: You raised a cairn under the open sky at Openfield and took the Choir's second vow.

routes.label: Crank the caretaker awake and ask it what it was told
The Archive: the order itself, with the city's seal
The last doctor's diary, and the clinic table that says how they went
Past the tunnel guard after dark, or by the way a child knows
Through the guard

sump.journal: The Marrs walked out of a cistern with a number on it when its pumps stopped and its door would not open: Cistern 4, under the glass south-east of Ninebridge, where two scavenger clans are being paid to dig toward a door. What the city told Cistern 4, it told Cistern 9. The proof is down there.

proof.journal: Cistern 4 was ordered to send its people to the city on a date, and could not, and had its water cut for not complying, and died in the dark with its door shut and its records filed for return. The same order sits sealed in MOTHER's log three times over, refused. The cisterns were never anyone's but the city's. The city is east, and the map's road runs into it.

decision.text: You found in Cistern 4 what the city ordered of the cisterns.

news.text: someone went down the Sump's tunnel to the dead cistern and came back up with paper

routes.label: The runner's ledger: both rims paid from one purse
Put the ledger in front of both chiefs
Take a cut of the purse and let them dig
Take a side and clear the other rim

rims.journal: Two clans over one tunnel, paid on the fourth day to dig toward the same door and to hate each other in between. The guild's runner sleeps on the south rim with the purse.

objectives.text: Find out who pays the Sump
End the feud, or use it

united.journal: Grel and Hesk Tanner read the same ledger at the same fire and did not speak for a while, and then went together to the south rim. The runner left in the night with his purse and without his horse. The Sump digs for itself now, both rims, and the tunnel is open to anyone it does not mind.

news.text: the two clans at the Sump threw out the guild's runner and dig for themselves

grel.journal: The east rim is empty. Grel's people have both cabins and the tunnel and the purse, and the guild pays one column now instead of two, which Factor Pike will call a saving.

decision.text: You cleared the Tanners off the Sump's east rim for Grel.

news.text: Grel's clan took the whole Sump; a stranger's gun was in it

tanner.journal: The west rim is empty. Hesk Tanner has the cabins, the tunnel, the purse and the door, which is what Hesk Tanner wanted; the guild pays one column now.

decision.text: You cleared Grel's clan off the Sump's west rim for Hesk Tanner.

news.text: the Tanners took the whole Sump; a stranger's gun was in it

skim.journal: A tenth of the purse comes to you on the fourth day, and both rims keep digging, and hating, and neither knows why the runner looks at you when he counts.

decision.text: You took a cut of the guild's purse at the Sump and let the clans keep feuding.

routes.label: Carry the last doctor's letter to the city it was written to

carry.journal: The last doctor of Cistern 4 wrote the end of it in a clinic ledger, and addressed the last page to whoever came from Meridian. Nobody came. You have it. The city is east.

objectives.text: Put the diary in front of someone in Meridian who should read it

delivered.journal: Read, in the city it was written to. What that changes is the city's to decide.

routes.label: Stand the citizenship hearing and talk your way to papers
The hearing takes evidence: a guild ticket, a reserve's records, a dead doctor's letter
The scanner's file can be edited by someone who knows how
The storm drain under the wall, south of the gate
Push through with the crowd when it pushes
The file says ADMIT ON SIGHT. Let it

wall.journal: Meridian: the Wall, the gate, and the Ledger behind it that keeps a face for everyone it has ever seen. The map's road runs through the gate to the towers; so does the city's interest in a cistern that would not comply. There is a hearing for people without papers, and a line for the hearing, and a lens before the line.

objectives.text: Settle what you are to the Precinct

cells.journal: A cell in the warden station, tile floor, a cot, a fence door. The Precinct has a procedure for you and is following it. Someone will come; the file will say who.

inside.journal: Inside the Wall, with a status the Precinct can read off a card — or a storm drain and no card at all. The city knew your face before you gave a name; the file calls you something the clerk had never seen. The records office will know what. So will the assessor who keeps it.

decision.text: You got inside Meridian's Wall.

news.text: someone from the salt cut came through the Precinct gate and the lens knew their face

routes.label: Five questions on the charter, the drains and the calendar; three right makes a citizen

sit.journal: The records office sets an exam for provisional residents: five questions on the charter, the drains and the Restoration Calendar. Three right and the card is yours. The assessor says the questions are the same every year; it has filed a complaint about that.

passed.journal: Three of five, or better. A citizen of the Precinct, by examination, which the assessor says is the only lawful way and the least used.

routes.label: Pay forty-five for three things you have not done
Contest them at the Court of Accounts, by appointment

notice.journal: The Precinct has fined you for three offences, each with a forecast date: a curfew you will break, an avenue you will loiter on, an assembly you will attend. Forty-five Tolls, payable at the warden's counter. The desk warden was apologetic about the dates.

objectives.text: Pay the fines, or contest them

paid.journal: Paid. The receipt is stamped twice. You are, for the moment, a person the Precinct has no complaint against, including the ones it has not had yet.

contested.journal: Contested. The Court of Accounts will hear it, by appointment, which the assessor says could be any time and will be when the schedule says.

routes.label: Follow the wire from the kiosk to where it drinks
The boy who feeds it knows what it eats
A tap on the city's wire is worth something to the Broker

name.journal: A pre-Burn kiosk on Old Market's east street that still talks, and said your name before you gave it, and said other things after: a number, a reserve, a chair, a date. A boy feeds it cells. Something feeds it names.

objectives.text: Find out how the kiosk knows faces
Decide what to do about it

cut.journal: The wire is cut where it left the lamp post. The kiosk sells fortunes now out of a memory forty years deep and no newer, and gets everyone's name wrong, and the boy says it is happier.

decision.text: You cut the kiosk's tap on the city's wire.

sold.journal: The Broker bought the splice: a tap on the Precinct's lamp wire, which is a tap on the file. The kiosk still talks. So, now, does the hatch.

decision.text: You sold the Broker a tap on the city's file.

left.journal: You left the kiosk talking. It knows your name and the date, and will tell anyone who stands in front of it with two Tolls.

reported.journal: The wardens took the wire and the kiosk, and the boy, for an hour, and Captain Lowe wrote it up as an unlicensed tap and filed it where the Saints of Static will find it when it is their turn.

decision.text: You reported the kiosk's tap to the wardens.

routes.label: Talk the square down before the wardens count it
Bring the captain the count: point eight on the notice, point six on the dial
Stand with the queue when it goes for the dial
Let it run, and take what runs loose

queue.journal: The standpipe square in Old Market: the notice says point eight and the dial says point six, and forty people in a queue have done the arithmetic. Two wardens are counting them. Something will happen at the dial before dark.

talked.journal: The square sat down. You gave them the arithmetic and a place to send it, and Caddo Vell took the count to the Precinct himself with forty names on it, which is a petition and not a riot and gets a notice instead of a club.

news.text: Old Market's standpipe queue sent a petition to the Precinct instead of breaking the dial

lowe.journal: Captain Lowe came down to the square himself with the notice in his hand, read both numbers aloud, and turned the dial to point eight with his own fingers while the queue watched. He checked the arithmetic. It was wrong. He wrote that down.

news.text: the warden captain came to Old Market and turned the water dial up himself

crowd.journal: The queue went for the dial and you went with it, and the two wardens went down under forty people and were let up again, and the dial is broken open and the standpipe runs. The Precinct will count this one carefully.

decision.text: You stood with Old Market's queue when it broke the water dial.

news.text: Old Market broke its water dial; a stranger was in the front of it

loot.journal: It ran. The dial went, the wardens went for help, the crates at the square's edge went in the confusion, and so did you, with what was in them. The queue drinks; the Precinct counts; nobody saw you.

decision.text: You let Old Market riot and took what ran loose.

taken.journal: A flat steel case for the clerk at the Exchange in Ninebridge, by hand, unopened. Sixty on delivery, the board says. It ticks, faintly.

paid.journal: Sixty Tolls through the hatch, and a hand you did not see take the receipt.

q_gig_meds.title: Gig: Knit Kits for the Farms

taken.journal: Two knit kits for the sick hall at Openfield, where the Choir's healer is short. Fifty, the board says, and the Choir's thanks, which the Broker does not pay in.

paid.journal: Fifty through the hatch. The healer at Openfield has two knit kits she did not have.

taken.journal: A debt contract on the block at Ninebridge: lot seven, a mechanic, forty-eight. The Broker wants the paper, and fronts nothing. A hundred and twenty for it, the board says; the lot opens at seventy.

paid.journal: A hundred and twenty through the hatch for the mechanic's paper. Whoever he is, he is the Broker's now, and the Broker says that is better than the block, and is probably right.

q_gig_letter.title: Gig: A Letter for the Captain

taken.journal: A sealed letter for Captain Lowe at the Precinct station, by hand. Twenty, the board says. It is the weight of a letter with something flat inside.

paid.journal: Twenty through the hatch. "He always refuses," the voice box said. "The point is that he knows who asked."

q_gig_box.title: Gig: A Box from the Sump

taken.journal: A boxed piece of chrome in the Tanners' locker at the Sump, which the Broker says is the Broker's and the Tanners say is the Tanners'. Eighty for it through the hatch.

paid.journal: Eighty through the hatch, and the box gone into the container without a sound.

routes.label: A variance under clause 14: the Precinct bears the shortfall (the assessor, or the captain)
Retime the relief pumps at the dial
Take the pump house with the Pale

rising.journal: The first pier of the Sink's stilt-walk has a chalk line for every spring, each a hand above the last, and next spring's already drawn with a question mark. Something is pumping, far off, for somebody else.

objectives.text: Learn what the pumps are told to do in spring
See the Sink through the spring

paid.journal: A variance under clause 14, the drains being the city's first duty: the relief pumps run for the Sink this spring and the Precinct bears the shortfall. Dagny Roos read it twice and turned her own dial, which she has not been allowed to do in eleven years. The Precinct will drink point six and notice.

decision.text: You had the Sink's relief pumping varied under clause 14; the Precinct bears the shortfall.

news.text: the Sink's pumps will run this spring on a variance; the Precinct's ration drops to pay for it

retimed.journal: The relief dial reads what you set it to. Two pumps that were the Precinct's in spring are the Sink's again, and the seal on the dial is a seal on a dial, which the wardens will find out when they next count. Dagny Roos says she does not know who did it, which is nearly true.

decision.text: You retimed the Sink's relief pumps behind the Plan's seal.

news.text: somebody retimed the Sink's pumps under the Plan's seal; the Precinct's pressure dropped overnight

seized.journal: The Pale hold the pump house. The wardens who held it are on the tally wall, by the Pale's hand and yours, and the pumps run for the Sink because Saskia Dray says so. The Precinct will come down the stair for this, in its own time, with its own count.

decision.text: You took the Sink's pump house from the Precinct with the Pale.

news.text: the Pale took the Sink's pump house from the wardens; a stranger was in it

routes.label: Buy one from Vash's cold box, and don't ask
Take it from the Pale's cold store
A dark-chrome Second Heart instead, and Ocho to fit it

need.journal: Tam Oduya pumped the Sink for the Precinct for eleven years and the wet got into his heart. Ocho can fit a new one — a real one, chilled, or a dark-chrome Second Heart — if one comes through the clinic door. Vash sells hearts. Nobody says whose.

objectives.text: Bring Ocho a heart he can fit

fitted.journal: Tam Oduya has a heart that beats. Ocho asked where it came from and you told him, and he asked Tam, and Tam said yes before the sentence was finished. The Code says the patient decides. It does not say Ocho has to like it.

fitted_chrome.journal: Tam Oduya has a Second Heart under his ribs, Mender-built, no leash. It does not skip. He says it ticks, and that he can live with ticking.

fitted_lie.journal: Tam Oduya has a heart that beats and a number inked on a bag in Ocho's bin, crossed out. Ocho believes it came from under the water. You know whose walk it came off.

hands.journal: Ocho does not take apprentices; he takes hands. Hold a clamp steady through one fitting and he will say the words, which are: *fit only what the patient can bear*. Shake, and Pell takes the clamp, and there is always a next time down here.

objectives.text: Hold steady through a fitting at Ocho's table

apprentice.journal: Apprentice, by the Menders' Code. Ocho said the words over a table with a man still open on it, which Pell says is how he says everything. Menders' prices are yours now, where there are Menders, and so is the thing the Code asks: fit only what the patient can bear.

routes.label: Read the undercard before the house does
Stand against Anvil: hands and iron, nobody dies
Take the house's sixty to fall in the second

card.journal: Lantern Row's pit: Teague against Doubt on the undercard at two to one, and Anvil against all comers — thirty to enter, ninety if you are standing at the end. Nobody has stood since spring. Mab Corrigan keeps the slate and the guns.

objectives.text: Stand against Anvil, or fall for the house

standing.journal: Standing, at the end, with Anvil on the floor he keeps so clean and the crowd losing money by the fistful. Ninety from the cash-box, and a pit token the Skirts' pits and the Crown's will honour.

fallen.journal: Down in the second, as agreed, and sixty from Mab after, which on the Row counts as a deal kept. The crowd knew. The crowd always knows.

routes.label: Two hundred, because wardens
An hour on the cot: a memory of yours for his
The Lantern's locker, after hours

shelf.journal: The Lantern's evidence shelf holds a reel a Rustmouth took off a warden: a man with no face in it recorded his last day in the city, start to end, a season ago, and went west before dawn. Ysolde Marr wants two hundred for it, or something of yours.

objectives.text: Live his day, on a cot in the Lantern

seen.journal: You lived the stranger's last day in the city through his eyes: a long stair, something flat carried against the ribs, this cot, a bowl of noodles eaten standing, and a gate at dawn with somebody on the road beyond it who was waiting. What you made of it is in the notebook's leads.

routes.label: Key money: two hundred and fifty to the committee
Settle the roof and the committee gives it
Break the seal and move in

offer.journal: Flat 9-14 in Block Seven: two rooms, a stove, a bed the Marrs left, a window on the canyon. The committee wants two hundred and fifty in key money, or the roof settled so Nine is not dry at six. The door has a seal on it.

objectives.text: Get the flat, one way or another

home.journal: A flat of your own, nine floors up: a bed to rest in, a locker to keep things in, a table to write at, a door that locks from your side. The Loop is downstairs.

routes.label: A schedule: hours for the beds, hours for the trays (the committee, or the valve)
The beds: pull the pump's fuse, or turn the valve west
The trays: argue the committee into giving them the tank
Burn the trays with Ren, and fight the Twelves

roof.journal: Block Seven's roof: a tank that fills off the Precinct main at night, beds of real dirt on the Nines' side that are dry by noon, trays on the Twelves' side that take the whole tank from two to five. Nine old people and a tree against sixty dinners and a man in a clean coat. Three springs of committee pending.

objectives.text: Learn who takes what from the tank, and when

shared.journal: Five to two for the beds, two to five for the trays, in the keeper's log in capitals and in the committee's ledger with a date. Nine is wet at six and Twelve is green at eight. Nobody is happy and everybody is fed.

news.text: Block Seven's roof got a water schedule after three springs; the committee signed it

nines.journal: The pump is dead, or the valve is wired west; either way the tank is the beds' all night and the trays are drying. Sixty people will carry buckets. Lio Brand will remember the sum.

news.text: the Twelves' pump on Block Seven stopped; the Nines' beds are wet for the first time in three springs

twelves.journal: The committee gave the tank to the trays, out loud, in the ledger. Nine carries buckets from the laundry. Mama Deel has stopped coming to committee. A man in a clean coat was pleased, which should worry someone.

news.text: Block Seven's committee gave the roof tank to the hydroponic deck

burned.journal: The trays burned at two in the morning with the pump loud, and sixty dinners with them, and Nessa Kord's hands. The Twelves came across the deck with pipes. Ren Ashby is sitting in the dirt with an empty can. The committee has written your name beside his.

routes.label: Pay the Rustmouths' tithe and hold their chain against the Gilt, with a word or with iron
Bring the Gilt the Rustmouths' warden-stamped ledger, and pull the chain down with them
A sit-down under the Saints' mast: the chain split three ways before the Crown takes it

three.journal: Bridgeward: one chain across a bridge to nowhere, three paints on every wall. The Rustmouths hold the chain and collect a Tenured house's toll on it; the Gilt want it; the Pale say the bridge is nobody's and keep a hatch to the Sink. A woman in a clean coat holds the pen on the arrangement, and a girl at the Saints' tower says the Crown takes the near end by the Long Night.

objectives.text: Decide the chain: hold it, take it, or share it

rustmouths.journal: The Rustmouths hold the chain and you are a mouth on it, with a cut of a toll that goes nowhere. The Gilt went back to their fire barrel. The Crown's paper is the same paper it was.

gilt.journal: The chain is on the ground and the slate says STAND — FREE — GILT in gold, and the Rustmouths who held it are on the tally of a street that keeps no tally. Pip Aldous is coming down the Loop to see it. The Crown's agent has stopped coming Tuesdays.

peace.journal: Two Tolls to stand, split three ways, with a Gilt, a Rustmouth and a white hand at the chain together and nobody liking it. The girl said the Crown takes the near end by the Long Night. Three crews on one chain is the only thing it cannot take.

routes.label: Swear on the hiss: she stays sixteen, and the Saints tell you what the wire says
Give the warden captain the tower
Sell the Exchange its leak
Tell the Concern's man where a radio that works sits

hiss.journal: A girl at the Saints' tower in Bridgeward says the city's lines in the city's voice — reserve nine, point six, Thursday, a hand higher — and what she says comes true. The wardens would call her a tap, the Exchange a leak, the Concern a find. Verity wants her to be sixteen.

kept.journal: She stays at the altar, sixteen, saying the city's lines to forty dead radios. You swore on the hiss. When the wire says something you need, Verity will tell you, and nobody else.

silenced.journal: Wardens came for the tower at dusk with the captain at their head and took the girl to a cell with a blanket and no radio. Lawful. The altar has a gap in it and the Saints have your name.

news.text: wardens took the Saints' girl who hears from the Bridgeward tower

sold.journal: Guild riders came at dawn with a sealed sheet with her name on it, and she went to wherever the Exchange keeps the things it sells. The floor thanked you. The floor always thanks you.

news.text: guild riders took the Saints' girl who hears from the Bridgeward tower

concern.journal: A man in a clean coat came with a radio that worked and she went with him, and by Thursday she will have something in her neck and hear everything, all of it, all the time. Verity could keep one thing from her. Now she cannot.

news.text: a man in a clean coat took the Saints' girl who hears up the Loop

garage.journal: A garage in Bridgeward with a dog's head burned into every wall: the Rust Dogs' old haunt, before the Rustmouths took the bridge and the Dogs took the Sallow. An old Dog named Fenn has sat on the same bench for nine years, and the bench is a cache.

objectives.text: Open the cache under Fenn's bench

cache.journal: The cache under Fenn's bench: a revolver, cartridges, eighty Tolls and a strip of cloth with a dog's head on it, from when the Dogs were a crew. BACK FOR THE BRIDGE, the wall says, every spring. Fenn says the rope is what the bridge is for, and the Rustmouths keep one on the booth.

routes.label: Speak for a house at the Committee's lectern
Stand for a house on the floor: the Chair follows the duel
The house records its sittings as art; play the room a reel it was not in
A cup, at the toast. Nobody up here asks what was in a cup

lift.journal: The Loop's invitation car goes up to the Crown and costs nothing. At the top a lens and a sergeant decide what they have seen: a chit, a pass, a card, standing, a face the lens has filed, or clothes that say you belong. The help goes round the back. It is House Vane's season, and the Committee's Chair is decided at the toast.

terraces.journal: The terraces under glass. Two houses want the Chair: Vane, whose season it is and who has a man from the Concern at the back of her hall, and Ashby-Crane, who has sold nothing in ninety years and has no one to stand for her. The Chair signs the road, the bridge's near end, and the Committee's forecasts, which a Chair may sell on. The file is not in doubt; only the room.

objectives.text: Decide the Chair, or let the houses

vane.journal: The Chair went to House Vane, as the file expected. The road to the Docks will be voted, the bridge's near end signed for, and the Committee's forecasts go wherever Celestine Vane sends them. The Concern's man went down the lift before the toast, satisfied.

ashby.journal: The Chair went to House Ashby-Crane, against the file. Ninety years and nothing sold, and now a Chair. The Concern's man went down the lift without the toast. Celestine Vane turned her cup a quarter turn and said there would be another season.

exposed.journal: The room heard a room it was not in: House Vane's terms with the Concern, aloud, at the toast. The Chair went to Ashby-Crane and the Crown turned, all at once, politely, on Celestine Vane and on you. The lens filed every face. Yours is on a list up here now that has nothing to do with the sash.

mourning.journal: Celestine Vane took ill at her own toast and was dead before the car went down. The Committee met in the morning with the chair beside her table empty and voted the way frightened people vote: Ashby-Crane. Lawful, the wardens said. Nobody up here asks what was in a cup.

routes.label: Take her down the service lift as she paid for
Sell the house her escape; the house pays better than the hatch
Stand beside her while she tells her mother, and talk the marriage off

gig.journal: A Broker's gig off the Old Market board: a daughter, out of the Crown, down to the Row, two hundred; a kitchen pass for the service lift comes with it. Nobody at the hatch said kidnapping. Nobody at the hatch says anything.

objectives.text: Find the daughter in the Crown

daughter.journal: Ottilie Ashby-Crane paid the Broker herself, with money Osric Vane gave her, to be taken out of a marriage that seals the Chair. Her mother will pay three hundred to keep her. The service lift goes down at four with the rubbish and anyone in a kitchen coat with their head down.

objectives.text: Take her down, sell her back, or stand beside her

row.journal: She went down the service lift in a kitchen coat and is at the Velvet in a Row dress that fits her badly, tasting things. Her mother knows where she is and has sent nobody, which is the kindest thing she has ever done. The hatch owes you two hundred.

sold.journal: Her mother paid three hundred for the lift and the hour. The window in the salon is empty; Miss Ottilie is in her room, and will be. The hatch pays for results, and will not pay for this one.

stays.journal: Her mother said off. The marriage, the seal on the Chair, the sixty years under glass. Ottilie Ashby-Crane is still at the window, but she is sitting, and the dress is plainer, and she might go down anyway, with a house behind her, which is different.

portraits.journal: A studio on the Crown's terraces hung with portraits of people as they will be: older, finished, in the chairs their forecast sheets say, with dates under them that have not happened. The machine is on the city's wire. It is never wrong about a face. It has your name at the top of its queue, unrequested.

objectives.text: Decide what to do with your print

shown.journal: Halden looked at the photograph and would not touch it. Not his: the original, the city's own hand, no grain because there was no light. Nobody took it. It was expected. He will render you for fifty, if you want to see it printed warm.

objectives.text: Decide what to do with your print, or leave it in the drawer

print.journal: The renderer had you already, the day you came through the gate: the steps, the sash, the date. Halden printed it once then for nobody, because the machine told him to. What you did with the print is done, and the machine will print it again, because it always does.
